reconcile.note: Gill reads the sweeping grant of every tree in Genesis 1:29 as already carrying the single exception that Genesis 2:17 later spells out by name.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Richard Elliott Friedman treats the unrestricted grant in Genesis 1 and the single prohibition in Genesis 2 as evidence of two once-independent creation narratives, P and J, spliced together rather than one author's unified rule.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Richard Elliott Friedman, Who Wrote the Bible? (1987).

sides.snippet: Behold, I have given you every herb yielding seed, which is on the surface of all the earth, and every tree, which bears fruit yielding seed. It will be your food.
sides.verseText: God said, \"Behold, I have given you every herb yielding seed, which is on the surface of all the earth, and every tree, which bears fruit yielding seed. It will be your food.

sides.snippet: but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, you shall not eat of it: for in the day that you eat of it you will surely die.
sides.verseText: but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, you shall not eat of it: for in the day that you eat of it you will surely die.\"
